candidates.title: Pair natural-language descriptions with positive/negative examples for regex synthesis
candidates.rule: When building a regex-generation component, require both an English description and positive/negative string examples, and use the description to constrain the search over example-consistent regexes, instead of relying on either modality alone.
candidates.passage: Among 322 regex tasks, Regel solves 80% of the benchmarks but DeepRegex solves only 43% and the PBE-baseline solves only 26%.
candidates.finding: On 200 adapted DeepRegex benchmarks and 122 StackOverflow benchmarks, the multi-modal system (semantic-parser sketch + example-guided search) solved 80% within up to four example-adding iterations, versus 43% for the NL-only seq2seq baseline and 26% for the examples-only variant of the same engine. Gains were largest on the harder StackOverflow set (60.7% vs 2.4% and 14.7%).
models: SEMPRE-based semantic parser (log-linear model, beam size 500)
workloads: Adapted DeepRegex data set (200 benchmarks, ~4 positive and ~5 negative examples each)
StackOverflow regex data set (122 curated benchmarks)
candidates.conditions: Time budget 10s/top-1 for DeepRegex set, 60s/top-5 for StackOverflow set; top 25 parser sketches run in parallel; accuracy counted over up to four iterations where two disambiguating examples are added after each failure; StackOverflow sketch training labels were hand-written and posts were manually cleaned.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, pre-LLM components; fixed regex DSL; StackOverflow benchmarks were pre-processed and ground truth hand-translated; manual sketch annotation effort is not costed; failure cases involve high-level concepts (dates, ranges) the parser cannot represent; absolute accuracy on realistic tasks is only ~61%.
candidates.validation_test: On a held-out set of regex tasks with descriptions plus examples, compare three pipelines under matched compute: description-only generation, examples-only search, and description-constrained search; score exact-language equivalence of the top-k output against ground truth.

candidates.title: Iterate with counterexamples rather than accepting the first synthesis failure
candidates.rule: When a synthesizer returns a wrong regex, add two examples that specifically rule out the returned candidate and re-run, up to a small fixed number of rounds, rather than treating the first attempt as final.
candidates.passage: If it is unsuccessful, in the next iteration, we provide two additional examples that are guaranteed to rule out the returned incorrect regex .
candidates.finding: Using this iterative protocol on the DeepRegex set, the system went from 151/200 (75.5%) solved on initial examples to 185/200 (92.5%) after up to four rounds of adding two counterexamples each; the NL-only baseline cannot benefit since it ignores examples.
candidates.conditions: Maximum four iterations; counterexamples were constructed by the experimenters with knowledge of the ground truth, which a real user may not have; per-iteration average running time stayed within a few seconds (DeepRegex set) to ~20s (StackOverflow set).
candidates.limitations: The oracle-quality counterexamples inflate gains relative to real users; in the 20-person user study (5 engineers, 15 CS students) tool-assisted success was 73.3% vs 28.3% unaided, but tasks were StackOverflow posts, not the participants' own work, and ambiguity caused failures; single paper, no matched-budget comparison against simply running longer.
candidates.validation_test: Run the synthesizer under two protocols with equal total compute: single-shot, versus up to four rounds where each round adds two examples that the previous wrong output violates; report solved counts and cumulative time per protocol.

reason: The paper is a pre-LLM program synthesis system, but it contains tested comparisons that support scoped rules for harness design: combining natural-language specs with input/output examples rather than either alone, and using the NL-derived sketch structure to prune the example-based search. A third rule about iterative example-driven repair is also supported. All are specific to regex synthesis with a semantic parser and enumerative PBE engine, so scope must be kept narrow.
